hints.title: Reflect a height about y=1
hints.body: If the old height is y, its reflection y′ satisfies y+y′2=1. Therefore y′=2−y.
hints.recap: Reflection in a horizontal line <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></math> sends a height y to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></math>.
hints.pitfall: Reflection in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> is not simply negating the function.

recall.reminder: Reflection in a horizontal line <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></math> sends a height y to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></math>.

hints.title: Move the reflected graph horizontally
hints.body: Work with the formula you obtained after the reflection. To find a shifted graph value at a new horizontal coordinate, identify the old coordinate from which that point moved.
hints.recap: A rightward translation replaces a function’s input by the new coordinate minus the displacement.
hints.pitfall: Perform the transformations in the order stated.
hints.pause: Apply the horizontal shift to your reflected formula and check it using one original point.

recall.reminder: A rightward translation replaces a function’s input by the new coordinate minus the displacement.

solution:
Reflection about y=1 sends any height y to 2−y, because the average of the original and reflected heights is 1. Thus y=cosx becomes y=2−cosx.

Next translate by π4 in the positive x-direction. Replacing x by x−π4 gives y=2−cos(x−π4), option D.

The original maximum (0, 1) becomes a minimum at (π4, 1), and the transformed heights range from 1 to 3, confirming the reflection and translation.
knowledgePattern: Reflect in a horizontal line then translate horizontally
